title: Seller wargame play: sprint notebook (draft)
content:
Goal:
- Produce a lightweight slide/scene set that SEs and sellers can run through in a 20–30 minute rehearsal. Not a full deck, more of a pocket theatre: scenes, lines, counters, metrics to drop, and one-slide leave-behind.

Audience & usage notes:
- Primary: field SEs and solutions sellers prepping for pilot conversations with platform or product engineering personas.
- Secondary: SDRs for quick triage, CS for pilot handoff.
- Use format: 4 scenes (open, qualify, canary/scale, procurement) + 3 micro-battlecards (latency-first, cost-econ, compliance fallback). Each scene fits on 1 slide.

Structure (quick index):
1) Opening scene: 90s intro script + 2 empathy hooks
2) Qualify scene: 6 quick questions, eyes-on-deck cues
3) Canary/technical-run scene: demo cues, what to observe, rollback triggers
4) Procurement scene: pricing anchors and negotiation play
5) Battlecards: 3x one-paragraph counters + 2 rapid stats each
6) Leave-behind: single-slide value map + checklist

Scene 1 — Opening (90s):
- Objective: get alignment on who owns SLA and what “good” looks like in 2 metrics (p95 latency, monthly cost per 1M tokens).
- Script (SE): “Quick frame — we build inference as a runtime: our job is predictable latency, predictable unit economics, and graceful fallbacks. Before we dive, what’s the one metric you’d show your PM to prove the feature is production-ready?”
- Empathy hooks: “We’ll avoid replatforming your model infra” + “We can prove economics on a pilot before any long-term commit.”

Scene 2 — Rapid qualify (5–8 mins):
- Goal: identify signal to route to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Questions (ask in order):
  1) Expected peak RPS and p95 target?
  2) Sensitive data? (PII/regulatory?)
  3) Budget model: commit vs pay-as-you-go?
  4) SLO owner — app or infra?
  5) Multi-region requirement?
  6) Model update cadence?
- Cues for hosted fit: low to moderate sustained QPS, few regulatory constraints, need fastest time-to-value.
- Cues for dedicated/private: sustained high throughput, contractual SLA, or regulatory isolation needs.

Scene 3 — Canary & technical run (10 mins):
- Setup: small canary dataset, 20–30k tokens/day traffic, synthetic worst-case prompt (long context + grounding).
- Demo cues for SE (what to show):
  * Token-level latency trace (show p50/p90/p95 markers) — drop a red/green callout: p95 under target? green.
  * Cost per 1k tokens comparison: baseline model vs quantized variant.
  * Fallback in action: show how a heavier model drops into a cheaper quantized variant when queue >10s.
- Watch-for signals (immediate red flags):
  * KV cache miss rate >40% on repetitive prompts
  * Average inference batch size = 1 (indicates poor batching — discuss client integration)
  * Sudden token-cost spikes during long prompts (unbounded loop in app)
- Rollback triggers: non-deterministic hallucination regressions on golden prompts, sustained p95 > target for 5m, or error rate >1%.

Scene 4 — Procurement & pilot commitment (5 mins):
- Pricing anchors to present (quick):
  * Hosted: $X per 1k tokens (example anchor: $3.50 / 1k tokens for gen-tier model) + pilot credit offer
  * Dedicated: commit tiers (monthly GPUs) with throughput guarantees; show back-of-envelope 20–30% unit cost improvement at committed levels
  * Private: flat platform fee + support; we recommend for regulated orgs only
- Negotiation plays:
  * If asked for lower pilot price: offer time-limited pilot credit + success criteria (quality + latency)
  * If asked to waive SLA: require A/B rollback policy and canary phase to reduce risk

Battlecards (micro):
A) Latency-first persona (integration architect)
- One-line objection: “We can’t accept 250–300ms extra latency on user journeys.”
- Counter: “We map end-to-end budget: often network + client crush > model time. We instrument at token-level and suggest edge routing + micro-batching to shave 30–60ms; if not feasible, we provide a low-latency dedicated route with latency SLOs and fallbacks so user journeys stay intact.”
- Quick stats to drop: p95 reduction via batching/caching = up to 40%; dedicated route latency SLO target = 80–120ms on NVidiaH100-sized compute (example).

B) Cost-economist persona (FinOps)
- One-line objection: “Token cost will balloon at scale.”
- Counter: “Pilot to prove unit economics: we simulate monthly 10M-token workload across quantization and batching profiles; Optimize recommends quantized checkpoint that cuts cost by ~2–3x while preserving 95% of quality metrics.”
- Quick stats: expected unit cost delta (baseline vs 4-bit quant) = 2.4x; caching can reduce recurrent prompt token usage by 15–35%.

C) Compliance persona (security/regulatory)
- One-line objection: “We need full on-prem / air-gapped control.”
- Counter: “Private deployment with customer-managed control plane plus HSM/KMS integrations. For pilot, we propose a scoped PII redaction pipeline and audit logging enabled; if regulator still requires, escalate to private deployment track.”
- Quick stats: compliance maturity checklist (SOC2 in place, audit log retention configurable, KMS integration supported).

Leave-behind — single slide (one-paragraph + checklist):
- Paragraph: “Redwood Inference helps engineering teams turn LLM prototypes into predictable features. Our quick pilots prove latency & cost with measurable rollback-safe policies. For teams that need isolation, we migrate to dedicated/private with the same API and observability.”
- Checklist (for pilot sign-off):
  * Define p95 target and owner
  * Provide sample traffic + golden prompts
  * Agree success criteria: latency + cost per 1M tokens + quality score on evaluation set
  * Canary window length (recommend 48–72h)
  * Rollback plan agreed? (Y/N)

Open questions for the team (notes to self):
- Do we standardize numeric anchors for pricing or keep placeholders per account? (ask RevOps)
- Need a simple micro-dashboard template for SEs to screenshot during demos (token-level trace + cost delta) — who builds? (Product Ops?)
- Should we add a short script for SDRs to hand off to SEs with the 6 qualify questions embedded?

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Diego: build 1-slide leave-behind graphic (due 2025-11-28)
- Priya: confirm pricing anchors with RevOps + add ranges (due 2025-11-25)
- Evan: prototype micro-dashboard screenshot template (due 2025-12-02)
